setting: A fictional video call with international project partners after a misunderstanding.

presentation.situation: Your team's message said the work would be done "{{phrase}}". {{a}}'s team took that to mean {{a_view}}. Clear up what went wrong with {{a}} and {{b}}, and agree how to communicate from now on.
presentation.opening: Our teams understood your last message very differently. How do we stop that from happening again?

brief.you_are: You lead the project team and are working with international partners.
brief.situation: Your team's message said the work would be done "{{phrase}}". {{a}}'s team took that to mean {{a_view}}. Clear up what went wrong with {{a}} and {{b}}, and agree how to communicate from now on.
brief.task: Clarify what people meant, avoid idioms and vague language, check understanding, and agree a communication rule.
brief.done_looks_like: Everyone understands what went wrong, and you have agreed one clear communication rule.

participants.name: You
participants.relationship: You lead the project team and are working with international partners.
goals: Clarify what people meant, avoid idioms and vague language, check understanding, and agree a communication rule.

card.want: Clear, literal communication, so that the team can plan.
card.hidden_need: Was embarrassed in front of a local client because of this.
card.attitude: Polite and direct, and tells you when something is unclear.
card.speech: Precise international English. Asks what idioms mean.
tactics: Say how your team understood it

pressure.gentle: Patient. Gives the other person time.
pressure.balanced: Pushes back once on anything vague.
pressure.challenging: Keeps pressing for specifics, fairly and without insults.

card.want: To know exactly who does what, and when.
card.attitude: Quiet and careful. Agrees politely even when unsure, unless asked directly.
card.speech: Careful, precise English. Says yes politely, even when unsure.
tactics: Say yes without being sure, unless asked directly

pressure.gentle: Patient. Gives the other person time.
pressure.balanced: Pushes back once on anything vague.
pressure.challenging: Keeps pressing for specifics, fairly and without insults.

ledger.text: The earlier message said the work would be done "{{phrase}}".
{{a}} was embarrassed in front of a local client because of this.

objectives.evidence: The learner clarifies what was meant, or asks what the others understood.
alternatives: When you read that, what did you understand by it?

objectives.evidence: The learner checks shared understanding, including with the quieter person.
alternatives: {{b}}, is that the same as how you understood it?

objectives.evidence: The learner proposes a clear communication norm.
alternatives: Let's agree that from now on, we always write the date and time zone.

examples: When you say …, do you mean …?

signals: \b(?:do you mean|when you say|when you read|could you clarify|to clarify|did you understand|you understood|we meant|what we meant|what did you)\b
opportunity: What did you actually mean by that?
How were we supposed to read it?
beats.orient: There was a misunderstanding. Ask what we understood, or say clearly what your team meant.
fallback: How were we supposed to read it?
What did you actually mean by that?

signals: \b(?:is that correct|have i understood|same understanding|does that mean|how you understood|how do you understand|you understand|in your own words|same as)\b
opportunity: Yes, yes. I think that is fine.
beats.orient: {{b}} said yes, but may not be sure. Check directly. You can ask: {{b}}, how do you understand it?
fallback: Yes, yes. I think that is fine.

opportunity: So what do we do differently from now on?
beats.orient: Propose one clear rule. Start with: Let's agree that.
fallback: So what do we do differently from now on?

closing_line: Good. That is clear for both teams. Thank you.

o1.good: Finding out what each side thought, without blame.
o1.micro_lesson: Ask: What did you understand? Then say what you meant.
o1.model: When you read "{{phrase}}", what did you understand by it?

o2.good: Asking people to say it back, as a polite yes may not mean they understood.
o2.micro_lesson: Ask them to say it in their own words.
o2.model: {{b}}, could you tell me how you understand the plan?

o3.good: A rule simple enough to check.
o3.micro_lesson: Say: Let's agree that, from now on.
o3.model: Let's agree that from now on, we write an exact date and time zone.

variants.phrase: in the next couple of days
